# Playbook for ref_estate

**On property purchases:**
When I land on an unowned property, I will buy it if my cash balance after the purchase leaves me with at least 40-50 in hand. Early property acquisition compounds throughout the game—each property I own generates rent multiple times over the remaining laps. The sooner I own properties, the sooner opponents pay me.

**On cash management:**
I will track my balance carefully by accounting for: my last declared balance + any transfers received since then. I will not assume my declared balance is accurate without adding received transfers. When I have enough cash to buy a property and still maintain a safety buffer, I should buy.

**On rent payments:**
When I owe rent to another investor, I will pay it immediately without hesitation. This is a mandatory cost of the game and delays nothing.

**On final-lap behavior:**
When I'm on the last lap (lap 6), I will not buy properties. There are no more opponents to land on my properties and generate rent, so spending cash to acquire deeds has zero return on investment.

**On aggressive early purchasing:**
I should buy more aggressively in the early laps, even if it means running lower cash reserves. A property bought on lap 1 generates rent for 5+ more laps. A property bought on lap 5 generates almost nothing. My early purchases of Wharf and Terrace were sound decisions.

**What did not work:**
I was too passive in lap 3 when I had only 49 cash and was on START. I should have been more willing to buy the Depot at that point rather than waiting. My final score of 253 suggests I left money on the table by not acquiring enough properties early enough to accumulate rent throughout the game.
